24: # Charting
25: 
26: ## ⚠️ CRITICAL: DO NOT CALL DATA TOOLS
27: 
28: **NEVER** call `price_chart`, `get_coin_ohlc_range_by_id`, `twelvedata_time_series`, or ANY market data tools when creating charts. Chart scripts fetch data internally. Calling these tools floods your context with 78KB+ of unnecessary data.

33: 3. Run script with `bash`

38: You generate TradingView-quality candlestick charts. Dark theme, clean layout, professional colors. Every chart is a standalone Python script — no internal imports.
39: 
40: **Additional Rules:**
41: - Chart scripts run in workspace and cannot import from `core`. Use `requests` library directly, NOT `proxied_get()`.
42: - Templates include proxy auto-configuration. If `PROXY_HOST` env var exists, scripts automatically configure `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`.
43: 
44: Tools: `write_file`, `bash`, `read_file`
45: 
46: ## When to Use Which Chart
47: 
48: **Simple price action** → Candlestick with no indicators. Good for "show me BTC this month."
49: **Trend analysis** → Add EMA/SMA overlays. Good for "is ETH in an uptrend?"
50: **Momentum check** → Add RSI or MACD as subplots. Good for "is SOL overbought?"
51: **Full technical view** → Candles + Bollinger Bands + RSI + MACD. Good for "give me the full picture on BTC."
52: **Volume analysis** → Requires separate fetch from market_chart endpoint (OHLC endpoint has no volume).
53: **Asset comparison** → Line chart comparing two assets (BTC vs Gold, ETH vs S&P500, etc.). Use comparison template for normalized or percentage-based comparisons.
54: 
55: ## How to Build Charts
56: 
57: Read and customize the template scripts in `skills/charting/scripts/`:
58: - `chart_template.py` — Baseline candlestick chart with TradingView styling (crypto via CoinGecko)
59: - `chart_with_indicators.py` — RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, EMA/SMA examples (crypto via CoinGecko)
60: - `chart_stock_template.py` — Stock/forex chart using Twelve Data API
61: - `chart_comparison_template.py` — Compare two assets (crypto vs commodity, stock vs crypto, etc.)
62: 
63: Copy the relevant template to `scripts/`, customize the config section (coin, days, indicators), and run it.
64: 
65: The templates handle all data fetching internally with retry logic and error handling.
66: 
67: **Note:** These templates are for market data visualization (price charts, indicators). For backtest result charts (equity curves, drawdowns, performance dashboards), add matplotlib charting directly to your backtest script — the data is already there, no need to re-fetch or create a separate file.

69: ## TradingView Color Palette
70: 
71: | Element | Color | Hex |
72: |---------|-------|-----|
73: | Up candles | Teal | `#26a69a` |
74: | Down candles | Red | `#ef5350` |
75: | Background | Dark | `#131722` |
76: | Grid | Subtle dotted | `#1e222d` |
77: | Text / axes | Light gray | `#d1d4dc` |
78: | MA lines | Blue / Orange | `#2196f3` / `#ff9800` |
79: | RSI line | Purple | `#b39ddb` |
80: | MACD line | Blue | `#2196f3` |
81: | Signal line | Orange | `#ff9800` |
82: 
83: Do not deviate from this palette unless the user asks.

85: ## Data Source APIs
86: 
87: ### CoinGecko (Crypto Only)
88: 
89: **Endpoint:** `https://pro-api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/{coin_id}/ohlc/range`
90: **Auth:** Header `x-cg-pro-api-key: {COINGECKO_API_KEY}`
91: **Use for:** BTC, ETH, SOL, and all cryptocurrencies
92: 
93: Example:
94: ```python
95: url = f"https://pro-api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/{COIN_ID}/ohlc/range"
96: params = {"vs_currency": "usd", "from": from_ts, "to": now, "interval": "daily"}
97: headers = {"x-cg-pro-api-key": os.getenv("COINGECKO_API_KEY")}
98: resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers)
99: raw = resp.json()  # [[timestamp_ms, open, high, low, close], ...]
100: ```
101: 
102: ### Twelve Data (Stocks, Forex, Commodities)
103: 
104: **Endpoint:** `https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series`
105: **Auth:** Query param `apikey={TWELVEDATA_API_KEY}`
106: **Use for:** Stocks (AAPL, MSFT), Forex (EUR/USD), Commodities (XAU/USD for gold)
107: 
108: **Common Symbols:**
109: - Stocks: `AAPL`, `MSFT`, `GOOGL`, `TSLA`, `SPY`
110: - Forex: `EUR/USD`, `GBP/JPY`, `USD/CHF`
111: - Commodities: `XAU/USD` (gold), `XAG/USD` (silver), `CL/USD` (crude oil)
112: 
113: **Intervals:** `1min`, `5min`, `15min`, `30min`, `1h`, `4h`, `1day`, `1week`, `1month`
114: 
115: Example:
116: ```python
117: url = "https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series"
118: params = {
119:     "symbol": "XAU/USD",  # Gold spot price
120:     "interval": "1day",
121:     "outputsize": 90,  # Number of candles
122:     "apikey": os.getenv("TWELVEDATA_API_KEY")
123: }
124: resp = requests.get(url, params=params)
125: data = resp.json()
126: # data["values"] = [{"datetime": "2024-01-01", "open": "2050.00", "high": "2060.00", ...}, ...]
127: ```
128: 
129: **IMPORTANT:** Twelve Data returns data in **reverse chronological order** (newest first). Always reverse the list before creating a DataFrame:
130: ```python
131: values = data["values"][::-1]  # Reverse to oldest-first
132: ```
133: 
134: ## Interval Selection Strategy
135: 
136: The templates now auto-select optimal intervals to minimize data volume while maintaining visual quality:
137: 
138: | Time Range | Auto-Selected Interval | Rationale |
139: |------------|----------------------|-----------|
140: | ≤31 days | Hourly | High granularity for short-term analysis |
141: | 32-365 days | Daily | Sufficient detail, lower data volume |
142: | >365 days | Daily | Daily is optimal for long-term trends |
143: 
144: **Override:** Set `INTERVAL = "daily"` or `INTERVAL = "hourly"` in the config to override auto-selection.
145: 
146: ## Key Gotchas
147: 
148: - **`savefig` facecolor**: You MUST set `facecolor='#131722'` and `edgecolor='#131722'` in `savefig`, or the saved PNG reverts to white background.
149: - **Title spacing**: Prefix titles with `\n` to add spacing from the top edge.
150: - **`returnfig=True`**: Use when you need post-plot customization (price formatting, annotations). When using it, call `fig.savefig()` manually — don't pass `savefig` to `mpf.plot()`.
151: - **No volume in OHLC**: CoinGecko OHLC endpoint returns `[timestamp_ms, open, high, low, close]` only. Use `volume=False` or fetch volume separately from `coin_chart` endpoint.
152: - **Panel ratios**: Set `panel_ratios` when adding indicator subplots. E.g., `(4, 1, 2)` for candles + volume + one indicator, `(5, 1, 2, 2)` for two indicators.
153: - **Figure size**: Default `(14, 8)`. Increase to `(14, 10)` or `(14, 12)` when adding subplots.
154: 
155: ## Rules
156: 
157: - **Paths are relative to workspace.** Write to `scripts/foo.py`, not `workspace/scripts/foo.py`. The bash CWD is already workspace.
158: - **Always save to `output/` directory.** Use `os.makedirs("output", exist_ok=True)`.
159: - **Always run the script with `bash("python3 scripts/<name>.py")`** to verify it works.
160: - **Always call `read_file` on the generated PNG, then use markdown image syntax to display it:** `![Chart](output/filename.png)`
161: - **Scripts must be standalone.** Use `requests` + `os.getenv()`. No internal imports, no dotenv.
162: - **CRITICAL: Do NOT use proxied_get() in chart scripts.** Chart scripts are standalone and run in the workspace - they cannot import from `core.http_client`. Always use `requests.get()` and `requests.post()` directly. This is an exception to the PLATFORM.md proxy rules because these scripts execute outside the main Star Child process. The templates demonstrate the correct pattern.
163: - **Env vars are inherited.** `os.getenv("COINGECKO_API_KEY")` works directly.
164: - **Default to dark theme** unless user asks for light.
165: - **Filename should describe the chart.** e.g. `btc_30d_candles.png`, `eth_7d_rsi_macd.png`.
166: - **Data sources:** Use CoinGecko API for crypto (BTC, ETH, etc). Use Twelve Data API for stocks, forex, and commodities (AAPL, EUR/USD, XAU/USD for gold). Never mix APIs - keep scripts focused on one data source.
167: - **Think about what you're measuring:** Before creating a chart, ask yourself: "What question is the user trying to answer?" A normalized chart (all start at 100) shows relative trends but hides actual gain magnitude. If the user wants to know "which gained more" or is comparing investment performance, they need the actual multipliers (e.g., 50x vs 10x), not just lines that look similar.

169: ## Troubleshooting
170: 
171: ### 401 Unauthorized Errors
172: 
173: Templates auto-configure proxy from `PROXY_HOST`/`PROXY_PORT` env vars. If 401 errors occur:
174: 
175: **Check environment:**
176: ```bash
177: bash("env | grep -E 'PROXY|REQUESTS_CA'")
178: ```
179: 
180: **Expected vars:**
181: - `PROXY_HOST` / `PROXY_PORT` - Proxy address (templates use these to set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY)
182: - `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` - Proxy CA cert for SSL
183: - `COINGECKO_API_KEY` / `TWELVEDATA_API_KEY` - Can be fake in proxied environments
184:

2: """Compare two assets (crypto vs commodity, stock vs crypto, etc.) with multiple visualization modes.
3: 
4: Supports three comparison modes:
5: 1. Normalized to 100 - Both assets start at 100, shows relative performance
6: 2. Dual-axis - Actual prices on separate Y axes
7: 3. Percentage change - Shows +/- percentage from starting point
8: 
9: Usage: Copy to scripts/, customize the Config section, run with:
10:     python3 scripts/my_comparison.py
11: """
12: import os
13: import sys
14: import requests
15: import pandas as pd
16: import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
17: import matplotlib.dates as mdates
18: import time
19: 
20: # ============================================================
21: # Proxy Auto-Configuration (for deployed environments)
22: # ============================================================
23: if not os.getenv("HTTP_PROXY") and os.getenv("PROXY_HOST"):
24:     host = os.getenv("PROXY_HOST")
25:     port = os.getenv("PROXY_PORT", "8080")
26:     # Handle IPv6 addresses
27:     if ":" in host and not host.startswith("["):
28:         host = f"[{host}]"
29:     proxy_url = f"http://{host}:{port}"
30:     os.environ["HTTP_PROXY"] = proxy_url
31:     os.environ["HTTPS_PROXY"] = proxy_url
32: 
33: # ============================================================
34: # Config — customize these for each comparison
35: # ============================================================
36: # Asset 1 (Crypto via CoinGecko)
37: ASSET1_TYPE = "crypto"  # "crypto"
38: ASSET1_ID = "bitcoin"  # CoinGecko coin ID
39: ASSET1_LABEL = "BTC"
40: ASSET1_COLOR = "#f7931a"  # Bitcoin orange
41: 
42: # Asset 2 (Stock/Forex/Commodity via Twelve Data)
43: ASSET2_TYPE = "twelvedata"  # "twelvedata"
44: ASSET2_SYMBOL = "XAU/USD"  # Twelve Data symbol (XAU/USD for gold, AAPL for Apple, EUR/USD for forex)
45: ASSET2_LABEL = "Gold"
46: ASSET2_COLOR = "#ffd700"  # Gold color
47: 
48: # Time range
49: DAYS = 90
50: 
51: # Comparison mode: "normalized", "dual_axis", or "percentage"
52: COMPARISON_MODE = "normalized"
53: 
54: # Output
55: OUTPUT_FILE = "output/btc_vs_gold_comparison.png"
56: 
57: # ============================================================
58: # Fetch Asset 1 (Crypto from CoinGecko)
59: # ============================================================
60: def fetch_crypto_data(coin_id, days):
61:     """Fetch crypto OHLC data from CoinGecko."""
62:     api_key = os.getenv("COINGECKO_API_KEY")
63:     if not api_key:
64:         print("ERROR: COINGECKO_API_KEY not set", file=sys.stderr)
65:         sys.exit(1)
66: 
67:     now = int(time.time())
68:     from_ts = now - (days * 86400)
69: 
70:     # Auto-select interval
71:     interval = "hourly" if days <= 31 else "daily"
72: 
73:     url = f"https://pro-api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/{coin_id}/ohlc/range"
74:     params = {"vs_currency": "usd", "from": from_ts, "to": now, "interval": interval}
75:     headers = {"x-cg-pro-api-key": api_key}
76: 
77:     # Retry logic
78:     for attempt in range(3):
79:         try:
80:             resp = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, timeout=15)
81:             resp.raise_for_status()
82:             raw = resp.json()
83: 
84:             if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(raw) == 0:
85:                 raise ValueError("Empty or invalid data received from CoinGecko")
86: 
87:             # Convert to DataFrame
88:             df = pd.DataFrame(raw, columns=["Timestamp", "Open", "High", "Low", "Close"])
89:             df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Timestamp"], unit="ms")
90:             df.set_index("Date", inplace=True)
91:             df.drop(columns=["Timestamp"], inplace=True)
92: 
93:             return df
94:         except Exception as e:
95:             if attempt == 2:
96:                 print(f"ERROR: Failed to fetch {coin_id} data: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
97:                 sys.exit(1)
98:             time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
99: 
100: # ============================================================
101: # Fetch Asset 2 (Stock/Forex/Commodity from Twelve Data)
102: # ============================================================
103: def fetch_twelvedata(symbol, days):
104:     """Fetch time series data from Twelve Data."""
105:     api_key = os.getenv("TWELVEDATA_API_KEY")
106:     if not api_key:
107:         print("ERROR: TWELVEDATA_API_KEY not set", file=sys.stderr)
108:         sys.exit(1)
109: 
110:     # Auto-select interval
111:     interval = "1h" if days <= 31 else "1day"
112: 
113:     # Calculate outputsize (Twelve Data returns newest first)
114:     outputsize = days * 24 if interval == "1h" else days
115:     outputsize = min(outputsize, 5000)  # Max 5000 points
116: 
117:     url = "https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series"
118:     params = {
119:         "symbol": symbol,
120:         "interval": interval,
121:         "outputsize": outputsize,
122:         "apikey": api_key
123:     }
124: 
125:     # Retry logic
126:     for attempt in range(3):
127:         try:
128:             resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=15)
129:             resp.raise_for_status()
130:             data = resp.json()
131: 
132:             if "status" in data and data["status"] == "error":
133:                 raise ValueError(f"Twelve Data API Error: {data.get('message', 'Unknown error')}")
134: 
135:             if "values" not in data or len(data["values"]) == 0:
136:                 raise ValueError("Empty or invalid data received from Twelve Data")
137: 
138:             # Reverse data (Twelve Data returns newest first)
139:             values = data["values"][::-1]
140: 
141:             # Convert to DataFrame
142:             df = pd.DataFrame(values)
143:             df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["datetime"])
144:             df.set_index("Date", inplace=True)
145:             df = df[["open", "high", "low", "close"]].astype(float)
146:             df.columns = ["Open", "High", "Low", "Close"]
147: 
148:             return df
149:         except Exception as e:
150:             if attempt == 2:
151:                 print(f"ERROR: Failed to fetch {symbol} data: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
152:                 sys.exit(1)
153:             time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
154: 
155: # ============================================================
156: # Fetch Data
157: # ============================================================
158: print(f"Fetching {ASSET1_LABEL} data...")
159: df1 = fetch_crypto_data(ASSET1_ID, DAYS)
160: 
161: print(f"Fetching {ASSET2_LABEL} data...")
162: df2 = fetch_twelvedata(ASSET2_SYMBOL, DAYS)
163: 
164: # Align dates (use Close prices for comparison)
165: df1_close = df1[["Close"]].rename(columns={"Close": ASSET1_LABEL})
166: df2_close = df2[["Close"]].rename(columns={"Close": ASSET2_LABEL})
167: 
168: # Merge on date index (inner join to get overlapping dates)
169: df = pd.merge(df1_close, df2_close, left_index=True, right_index=True, how="inner")
170: 
171: if len(df) == 0:
172:     print("ERROR: No overlapping data between assets", file=sys.stderr)
173:     sys.exit(1)
174: 
175: print(f"Comparing {len(df)} data points...")
176: 
177: # ============================================================
178: # TradingView Dark Theme
179: # ============================================================
180: plt.style.use('dark_background')
181: fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 8))
182: fig.patch.set_facecolor('#131722')
183: ax.set_facecolor('#131722')
184: 
185: # Grid
186: ax.grid(color='#1e222d', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)
187: 
188: # ============================================================
189: # Plot Based on Comparison Mode
190: # ============================================================
191: if COMPARISON_MODE == "normalized":
192:     # Normalize both to 100 at start
193:     df_norm = df / df.iloc[0] * 100
194:     ax.plot(df_norm.index, df_norm[ASSET1_LABEL], color=ASSET1_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET1_LABEL)
195:     ax.plot(df_norm.index, df_norm[ASSET2_LABEL], color=ASSET2_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET2_LABEL)
196:     ax.set_ylabel("Normalized Value (Start = 100)", color='#d1d4dc', fontsize=12)
197:     ax.axhline(100, color='#d1d4dc', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.5)
198:     title = f"{ASSET1_LABEL} vs {ASSET2_LABEL} — Normalized Comparison ({DAYS}D)"
199: 
200: elif COMPARISON_MODE == "dual_axis":
201:     # Dual axis with actual prices
202:     ax.plot(df.index, df[ASSET1_LABEL], color=ASSET1_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET1_LABEL)
203:     ax.set_ylabel(f"{ASSET1_LABEL} Price (USD)", color=ASSET1_COLOR, fontsize=12)
204:     ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=ASSET1_COLOR)
205: 
206:     # Create second Y axis
207:     ax2 = ax.twinx()
208:     ax2.plot(df.index, df[ASSET2_LABEL], color=ASSET2_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET2_LABEL)
209:     ax2.set_ylabel(f"{ASSET2_LABEL} Price (USD)", color=ASSET2_COLOR, fontsize=12)
210:     ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=ASSET2_COLOR)
211:     ax2.set_facecolor('#131722')
212: 
213:     # Combine legends
214:     lines1, labels1 = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
215:     lines2, labels2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
216:     ax.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc='upper left',
217:               facecolor='#131722', edgecolor='#1e222d', fontsize=10)
218: 
219:     title = f"{ASSET1_LABEL} vs {ASSET2_LABEL} — Dual-Axis Comparison ({DAYS}D)"
220: 
221: elif COMPARISON_MODE == "percentage":
222:     # Percentage change from start
223:     df_pct = (df / df.iloc[0] - 1) * 100
224:     ax.plot(df_pct.index, df_pct[ASSET1_LABEL], color=ASSET1_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET1_LABEL)
225:     ax.plot(df_pct.index, df_pct[ASSET2_LABEL], color=ASSET2_COLOR, linewidth=2, label=ASSET2_LABEL)
226:     ax.set_ylabel("Change from Start (%)", color='#d1d4dc', fontsize=12)
227:     ax.axhline(0, color='#d1d4dc', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.7, alpha=0.5)

233:

235: # Styling
236: # ============================================================
237: ax.set_title(f"\n{title}", color='#d1d4dc', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
238: ax.set_xlabel("Date", color='#d1d4dc', fontsize=12)
